Class PolicyRetentionCriteria

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.context.reload.PolicyRetentionCriteria
All Implemented Interfaces:
RetentionCriteria
@Internal public final class PolicyRetentionCriteria extends Object implements RetentionCriteria
What a restart retains according to BeanRetentionPolicy beans: a singleton a policy retains, unless a change touched a configuration prefix one of the policies that retain it declares for it, and unless a policy refuses it, whatever their order. The context that stops also releases it when the change touched the prefix of a configuration bean in its closure, such as the @ConfigurationProperties it or its factory received, which no policy has to declare. A refusal also keeps a bean that holds the refused one from being retained, and the context that stops logs which policy refused.
Since:
5.3.0

graemerocher

    • observedConfigurationPrefixes

      public Set<String> observedConfigurationPrefixes(BeanRegistration<?> registration)
      Description copied from interface: RetentionCriteria
      The configuration prefixes a change under which releases a singleton this retains, as BeanRetentionPolicy.observedConfigurationPrefixes(BeanRegistration) declares them: a configuration bean under one of them that the singleton holds is not retained with it, nor does it keep it from being retained. A configuration bean of its closure under another prefix is observed instead, by RetentionCriteria.touches(String), so the prefixes only need to cover what the singleton reads outside configuration beans.
      Specified by:
      observedConfigurationPrefixes in interface RetentionCriteria
      Parameters:
      registration - The retained singleton's registration
      Returns:
      The prefixes, empty when only the configuration beans of its closure release it
